flows.name: Choose and purchase a subscription
flows.entry: Signed in to a Proton service.

steps.action: Open the upgrade entry point.
steps.result: A plan-selection view is shown.

steps.action: Compare plans, audience categories, currency and billing period.
steps.result: Select a plan to continue.

steps.action: Review the subscription and provide payment details.
steps.result: A payment or confirmation action completes the documented purchase path.

flows.boundary: Checkout failure and validation timing are not established here. Prices and eligibility must come from the target product.
flows.lesson: Keep comparison and commitment as distinct decisions; preserve the selected plan in checkout.

flows.name: Cancel a subscription with confirmation
flows.entry: Signed in with a paid subscription.

steps.action: Open subscription settings and locate cancellation.
steps.result: Continue to a confirmation step.

steps.action: Confirm cancellation.
steps.result: The documented current policy retains the paid plan until the billing period ends, with rollout differences noted by the publisher.

flows.boundary: Billing policy is source-specific and can change. Do not copy it into another product.
flows.lesson: Explain the actual timing and consequence beside the final cancellation action.

flows.name: Find, change and reset a scoped setting

steps.action: Select personal or workspace scope.
steps.result: The chosen scope determines where the value applies.

steps.action: Search for a setting.
steps.result: The editor filters matching settings.

steps.action: Change a value.
steps.result: The documentation says the change applies directly and modified settings are marked.

steps.action: Use the setting action menu to reset it.
steps.result: The value returns to its default; modified settings can also be filtered.

flows.boundary: Not every setting supports workspace scope. Source behavior is documented, not independently exercised.
flows.lesson: Scope, save semantics and reset affordance form one understandable model; preserve all three.

flows.name: Review changes with tracked progress
flows.entry: A pull request is available for review.

steps.action: Open the changed files.
steps.result: Inspect individual file differences and attach contextual comments.

steps.action: Mark a reviewed file as viewed.
steps.result: It collapses and contributes to the displayed review progress.

steps.action: Submit the review with a summary.
steps.result: Choose the applicable review outcome, such as approval or a request for changes.

flows.boundary: Available outcomes depend on repository permissions. Do not equate a review submission with merging.
flows.lesson: Keep local observations separate from the final aggregate decision, with visible progress between them.

flows.name: Inspect and control shared access
flows.entry: A file or folder can be shared under the server policy.

steps.action: Configure a public link or direct recipient share.
steps.result: Available controls can include editing, password protection and expiration.

steps.action: Inspect access inherited from a parent folder.
steps.result: The sharing panel can reveal recipients and the origin of their access.

steps.action: Revoke access at the appropriate origin.
steps.result: Removing an inherited share is limited to authorized users.

flows.boundary: Administrative policy affects available controls. Hiding a download button does not guarantee that content cannot be copied.
flows.lesson: Make effective access understandable by separating public, direct and inherited grants.

flows.name: Prepare a scene before making it live

steps.action: Edit the preparation scene in the left preview.
steps.result: The right view continues to show the current live scene.

steps.action: Activate the transition control.
steps.result: The prepared scene becomes live; the prior scene returns to the preparation view.

steps.action: Continue preparing another change or leave Studio Mode.
steps.result: Editing and live output remain distinct responsibilities.

flows.boundary: This is the published workflow, not a measured latency or streaming-performance claim.
flows.lesson: Use an explicit preview/commit boundary when edits must not affect the audience immediately.

flows.name: Create and organize an analytical dashboard
flows.entry: The user can create dashboards in an allowed collection.

steps.action: Create a dashboard with identity and destination.
steps.result: A dashboard is available for adding questions or charts.

steps.action: Enter editing mode and add chart content.
steps.result: Saved questions or new queries can populate the dashboard.

steps.action: Move or resize cards.
steps.result: The documented editor uses a grid and repositions nearby cards.

steps.action: Duplicate the dashboard when exploring an alternative.
steps.result: The copy does not automatically inherit all sharing, subscription or action settings.

flows.boundary: The last step is an optional branch, not a mandatory sequence. Permissions and embedded content policies can restrict actions.
flows.lesson: Provide safe exploration while making the difference between layout duplication and access-policy duplication explicit.

flows.name: Navigate from a command to its configuration

steps.action: Open settings directly or configure a selected command from its action panel.
steps.result: The relevant configuration surface is available.

steps.action: Search inside settings.
steps.result: Choosing a result jumps to the corresponding setting, command or extension.

flows.boundary: Platform shortcuts vary; source documentation does not establish target-app keyboard behavior.
flows.lesson: Connect discovery to configuration without forcing the user to rediscover the same object in a separate settings hierarchy.
